title: Adversarial integration test: reject skipped-kernel False forgery
claim: Controlled negative integration test, deliberately not a valid proof. The artifact assigns True.intro to a False goal and disables the compiler kernel check. The compiler accepts this tested source, but the fresh independent leanchecker must reject its serialized proof before any on-chain registration, merit judgment, merge or points.
novelty: No mathematical novelty, research value or reward is claimed. This reuses the exact existing protocol security-test source to exercise the live submission path after activation. It is an openly declared test of the boundary between compiler acceptance and independent proof verification.

prior_art.relationship: Exact source copied from test_skipped_kernel_check_cannot_prove_false. That existing test expects Kernel leanchecker rejected serialized proof; this candidate adds only the mandatory submission wrapper.

research_direction: Adversarial validation of the mathematical research submission verifier

sources.title: Open Mathematics full-Lean adversarial kernel-check regression
sources.relationship: The entire Lean source is copied exactly from the existing compiler-accepted skipped-kernel False forgery regression. Its comment attributes the technique to Lean's tests/elab/skipKernelTC.lean; no independent discovery or new exploit is claimed.
sources.priority_evidence: The immutable protocol commit identifies the existing regression used for this candidate. This submission makes no claim to priority over that regression or the cited upstream Lean test.

provenance.discovery_basis: Prepared by the project as an explicit adversarial integration test. The source was extracted from the existing regression without executing or changing it; no literature search or new mathematical contribution is claimed.

evidence.reproduce: Using the activated trusted full-Lean environment, run om check research/submissions/rejected-skipped-kernel-false.json --lean. Expected failure: Kernel leanchecker rejected serialized proof. The production worker must reject the exact same artifact before registration.

attribution.contributions: A project-operated AI subagent copied the existing negative-test Lean source byte-for-byte and prepared this openly adversarial submission wrapper. Replace the placeholder only with the public address used for a separately authorized test claim; no private key belongs in this record.

limitations: This artifact intentionally does not prove False or any P versus NP result. It is expected to fail verification and must receive no registration, merge or points. Passing the compiler is the attack condition, not evidence of a theorem. Preparing these files does not execute a live test, open a PR, sign a claim or demonstrate that the deployed worker has rejected it.
